body:
Additional visual-encoding findings, kept separate from the scene-type findings:

V12, blocking: feature terrain must not invent a second spatial dimension. Most features are defined over the one-dimensional surface axis or over discrete narrative supports. Spreading them across arbitrary Atlas y coordinates and drawing smooth contours can imply a continuous 2D gradient where none exists, especially when projection distance has no semantics. Safe defaults are an aligned track, exact interval or region fill, and local glyphs. Contours are scientifically natural in the true scale-space plane because x and window scale are declared axes. Elsewhere a terrain surface needs an explicit interpolation or extrusion recipe in AuditTrail and should be disallowed when the projection contract declares distance uninterpreted. Defer 2.5D elevation until this law is settled.

V13, blocking: fog or hatching cannot simultaneously mean uncertainty, missingness, boundary ambiguity, and model disagreement. These are different quantities and states. Missingness needs a reserved pattern or absence glyph; uncertainty needs an interval, band, or distribution-aware mark; boundary disagreement needs alternative boundaries; model disagreement needs split or juxtaposed analyses. Hatching can be one channel, but each meaning requires a distinct typed style and legend. Low magnitude must remain separate from all four.

V14: portal is a routing topology, not a relation type. Flashback, anticipation, retrospective mention, semantic recurrence, and distant causality may all use a nonlocal route, but they need typed arrowheads, endpoint glyphs, line patterns, or labels in addition to color. Likewise route, road, and thread require precise selection precedence when they overlap. The visual grammar should define channel ownership and collision rules, not only a symbol dictionary.

V15: animated projection changes are not themselves scientific geometry. Intermediate positions can violate discourse, temporal, and containment laws. Mark the application as transitioning, suspend geometry inspection or report both endpoint contracts during the animation, and evaluate laws only at committed scenes. Provide reduced-motion and immediate-switch modes. Preserve semantic FocusSet, not raw camera coordinates.

V16: Recall Voyage currently risks conflating mass, localization uncertainty, and visual blur. Blur is hard to measure and poor for precise comparison. Prefer a central route plus an uncertainty band or fan; use width only for declared alignment mass with a visible normalization basis; show unmatched or external mass explicitly so unbalanced transport still accounts for the full signature. Branches need posterior mass labels or a legend rather than looking like decorative alternatives.

V17: exact text round-trip needs its own visual and coordinate law. Canonical text uses UTF-16 offsets, while DOM selection crosses text nodes and normalized browser layout. The rail needs a deterministic offset-to-DOM index, tests for surrogate pairs and discontinuous SpanSet, and a rule for collapsed distant zoom that never destroys the source selection. Selecting one span may resolve to more marks than the viewport budget; the UI should preserve the semantic result set and aggregate offscreen marks instead of trying to draw everything.

V18: reproducible figures require deterministic label and font receipts. Cross-backend Scene determinism does not guarantee identical browser font metrics or label collision decisions. Record font asset and checksum, text measurement backend, label-ranking policy, collision solver version, and viewport size. Tile-local labels also need cross-tile collision and hysteresis rules or they will pop and reorder during pan.

These findings strengthen the core metaphor: cartographic feeling is welcome, but every apparent field, boundary, route, distance, and transition must have a declared construction and a truthful legend.
